places.name: The Dalí Museum
places.hours_text: Daily 10am–6pm, Thursdays until 8pm. Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.
places.price_text: Gallery admission: adults (18–64) $32; seniors 65+, educators, first responders and military $29; students (13–17 and college) $22; ages 6–12 $12; 5 and under free. Dome show add-on $15. Thursdays after 5pm: adults $16, ages 6–17 and college $10.
places.summary: Museum devoted to Salvador Dalí, built on the collection of A. Reynolds and Eleanor Morse; the museum says it holds over 2,400 works in every medium. Admission covers the galleries, special exhibitions and the Avant-garden; the Dalí Dome shows immersive projections for an added fee.
places.quote: The Dalí Museum celebrates the life and work of Salvador Dalí (1904-1989) and features works from the artist’s entire career.
places.accessibility: Galleries and the Will Raymund Theater are accessible for manual and electric mobility devices; 9 accessible parking spaces next to the museum; courtesy wheelchairs at the information station, first come, first served.
places.parking_text: On-site lot $10 (cards only), first come, first served; city garages, surface lots and street parking nearby.

places.name: Museum of Fine Arts, St. Petersburg
places.hours_text: Tuesday–Sunday 10am–5pm; Art After Dark on select Thursdays 5–8pm; closed Monday, Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.
places.price_text: Adults $16; seniors 65+, military, Florida educators and college students $14; youth 7–17 $10; 6 and under free.
places.summary: Art museum on the downtown waterfront, founded by collector Margaret Acheson Stuart and opened in 1965; the museum says it was the city's first art museum. The collection galleries are closed Sep 21–Nov 21, 2026 for a reinstallation; the New African Masquerades exhibition, shop and café stay open.
places.quote: The MFA opened to the public in 1965–the first art museum in the city.
places.status_note: Collection galleries temporarily closed Sep 21, 2026 and scheduled to reopen Nov 21, 2026 during the 'Reimagination'; the special exhibition, shop, café and programs continue (per mfastpete.org/about/reimagination, checked 2026-09-27).
places.parking_text: Paid self-parking in the south lot and along Bayshore Drive (Parkmobile or kiosk); garages and lots within walking distance.

places.name: Chihuly Collection
places.hours_text: Monday–Saturday 10am–5pm, Sunday noon–5pm. Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas; closes at 3pm on some holidays.
places.price_text: Adults $22; seniors 65+ and military $20; students (6–18 or college ID) $16; Museums for All $3; 5 and under free.
places.summary: Permanent collection of glass art by Dale Chihuly, run by the Morean Arts Center in a building designed for it. A ticket includes a live glassblowing demonstration at the Morean Glass Studio nearby.
places.quote: This presentation is unique as it is the first installation of Chihuly art in a building designed specifically for that purpose.
places.parking_text: Street parking and the 4th floor of the Publix parking garage during business hours.

places.name: Morean Arts Center
places.hours_text: Monday–Saturday 10am–5pm; closed Sunday and some holidays.
places.price_text: Gallery free.
places.summary: Contemporary art gallery and art school on Central Avenue with changing exhibitions and year-round classes. The same nonprofit runs the Chihuly Collection and the Morean Glass Studio nearby and the Morean Center for Clay in the Warehouse Arts District.
places.quote: The Morean Arts Center offers an amazing contemporary art gallery, FREE and open to the public daily PLUS affordable art classes year-round.
places.parking_text: Street parking and the 4th floor of the Publix parking garage during business hours.

places.name: Morean Glass Studio and Hot Shop
places.hours_text: Wednesday–Sunday noon–5pm. Live demonstrations Wednesday–Saturday at 12, 1, 2 and 3pm; Sunday at 1, 2 and 3pm.
places.price_text: Live glass demonstration $12, included with a Chihuly Collection ticket; personal glass experiences and classes priced separately.
places.summary: Glassblowing studio where resident artists work in front of visitors; the pieces are sold in the adjoining shop. You can also book a one-time hands-on glass experience or a class.
places.quote: Get behind the scenes and observe resident glass artists creating unique works of art.

places.name: Morean Center for Clay
places.hours_text: Wednesday–Saturday 10am–5pm; closed Sunday–Tuesday.
places.summary: Pottery center in a historic freight train depot in the Warehouse Arts District, home to more than 50 ceramic artists' studios, with classes and workshops. The Morean calls it the largest pottery studio in the Southeast.
places.quote: The largest pottery studio in the Southeast and one of the largest in the United States, the Morean Center for Clay is located in a historic freight train depot in the Warehouse Arts District of St. Petersburg.
places.parking_text: Free parking lot.

places.name: Imagine Museum
places.hours_text: Tuesday–Sunday 10am–5pm, Thursday until 8pm; closed Monday.
places.price_text: Adults $15; seniors 65+ and military $13; educators, college students and children 7–17 $10; members and 6 and under free.
places.summary: Museum of contemporary glass art from around the world, tracing the studio glass movement, with tours, scavenger hunts, a theater about glassmaking and a gift shop.
places.quote: Imagine Museum features a spectacular collection of contemporary glass art from around the world.
places.notes: The museum's own site (imaginemuseum.com) returned a SiteGround captcha to both curl and WebFetch on 2026-09-27, so the Visit St. Pete/Clearwater listing is the source; verifier should re-check hours and prices on imaginemuseum.com/plan-your-visit if reachable.

places.name: The James Museum of Western & Wildlife Art
places.hours_text: Daily 10am–5pm, Tuesdays until 8pm; last tickets 4:30pm (7:30pm Tuesday). Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.
places.price_text: General admission $23; seniors 65+ $18; students, teachers and active military $15; youth 7–18 $10; 6 and under free. Tuesdays: adults $10, youth $5.
places.summary: Museum of art of the American West and wildlife art: landscape paintings, sculpture, early Western art, Native American art and jewelry, and a wildlife gallery. Most of the art is on the second level.
places.quote: Showcasing sweeping landscape paintings and powerful sculptures that celebrate the land, people, and cultures of the American West.
places.parking_text: Levels 3 and 4 of the South Core Parking Garage behind the museum (enter at 101 1st Ave S), $2 per hour during regular operation.

places.name: Museum of the American Arts and Crafts Movement
aliases: Museum of the American Arts & Crafts Movement
places.hours_text: Tuesday–Saturday 10am–4pm, Sunday noon–4pm; closed to museum visitors Monday.
places.price_text: Adults $25; seniors 65+ $23; active military, students and educators $20; youth 6–17 $10; 5 and under free. Some seasonal exhibitions cost extra.
places.summary: Five-story museum founded by collector Rudy Ciccarello, devoted to the American Arts and Crafts movement (about 1890–1930): furniture, pottery, tiles, lighting, textiles and period rooms by Stickley, Frank Lloyd Wright, the Roycrofters, Grueby, Newcomb Pottery and others. It has a café, a store and a library.
places.quote: The Museum of the American Arts and Crafts Movement (MAACM) is the only museum in the world dedicated exclusively to the American Arts and Crafts movement.
places.status_note: The Fountain Garden is under construction for a gallery addition; follow signs for the temporary entrance (the 4th Street entrance is not wheelchair accessible), per the museum's visitor information page.
places.accessibility: Free wheelchairs at the admissions desk (a state ID is held as deposit); the 4th Street entrance is not wheelchair accessible during construction.
places.parking_text: MAACM Parking Garage next to the museum at 350 3rd Street North, $1 per hour; metered street parking nearby.

places.name: St. Petersburg Museum of History
places.hours_text: Monday–Saturday 10am–5pm, Sunday noon–5pm. Closed Thanksgiving, Christmas and Easter.
places.price_text: Adults $17; seniors 65+ $14; military and veterans $11; teachers, students and children 7–17 $9; 6 and under free.
places.summary: History museum at the entrance to the St. Pete Pier, with exhibits on the world's first commercial airline (including a replica of the Benoist airboat), 150 years of baseball in Schrader's Little Cooperstown and the history of tourism in the city. Perry's Porch restaurant is attached.
places.quote: Located at the entrance to the spectacular Pier District, the Museum of History has shared stories of the Sunshine City for a century.
places.parking_text: Metered St. Pete Pier Dolphin lot next to the museum, the Pelican lot, Pier street parking, or the Sundial garage (117 2nd Street N).

places.name: The Florida Holocaust Museum
places.hours_text: Daily 10am–5pm; last admission 4pm. Closed on listed holidays.
places.price_text: General $25; seniors 65+, educators, students, active-duty military, law enforcement and veterans $18; 6 and under free; Museums for All free.
places.summary: Museum of the Holocaust in downtown St. Petersburg, begun in 1992 by businessman Walter P. Loebenberg and in its current building since 1998. It calls itself one of the largest Holocaust museums in the country.
places.quote: The Florida Holocaust Museum honors the memory of millions of innocent men, women and children who suffered or died in the Holocaust.
places.accessibility: ADA compliant and fully accessible; free wheelchairs at the admissions desk; limited accessible parking on the north side of the building along the alley.
places.parking_text: Limited free parking at the museum; metered and free street parking and garages nearby. SunRunner stops at 5th Street South / 5th Street North.

places.name: The Woodson African American Museum of Florida
aliases: Dr. Carter G. Woodson African American Museum
places.hours_text: Tuesday–Saturday noon–5pm.
places.price_text: Free admission.
places.summary: Museum of African American history in the former community center of Jordan Park, which the museum describes as St. Petersburg's first African American public housing community. Its Legacy Garden shows the sculpture 'Harriet Tubman: The Beacon of Hope'.
places.quote: The Woodson African American Museum of Florida’s current building was previously the community center and an administrative office for the Jordan Park community
places.status_note: Closed from Monday, Sep 21, 2026 for scheduled roof maintenance; regular hours resume Tuesday, Sep 29, 2026 (per woodsonmuseum.org, checked 2026-09-27).

places.name: Great Explorations Children's Museum
places.hours_text: Monday–Saturday 10:30am–4pm, Sunday noon–4pm. Closed Easter, July 4, Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day and New Year's Day.
places.summary: Hands-on children's museum next to Sunken Gardens, with a preschool, camps and birthday parties.
places.quote: A place where kids can be creative, make discoveries and have fun!
places.notes: greatex.org returned a bot-check (HTTP 202, empty body) to curl and WebFetch on 2026-09-27; admission prices were not verified on a page we could read, so price_text is null.

places.name: Florida CraftArt
places.hours_text: Monday–Saturday 10am–5:30pm, Sunday noon–5pm; open later for the Second Saturday ArtWalk.
places.price_text: Free admission to the galleries.
places.summary: Statewide nonprofit for Florida fine craft, founded in 1951, with a gallery of work by more than 200 Florida artists (ceramics, glass, jewelry, wood and more) and an exhibition gallery with about ten shows a year, in the former Rutland's Department Store building.
places.quote: Florida CraftArt presents ten exhibitions annually, at no charge to the public, ensuring barrier-free access to the arts for all.
places.notes: Second Saturday closing time differs on the site (8pm on the home page, 9pm on About), so no time is given.

places.name: The St. Pete Pier
places.hours_text: Opens 30 minutes before sunrise, closes 11pm. Marketplace Friday–Sunday 10am–6pm (seasonal).
places.price_text: No charge to enter the Pier District; some special events are ticketed.
places.summary: Pier district on Tampa Bay with restaurants and a rooftop bar, public art, a playground and splash pad, Spa Beach, a fishing deck, a marketplace, the Tampa Bay Watch Discovery Center and free trams. The St. Petersburg Museum of History sits at its entrance.
places.quote: There is no charge to enter the Pier District.
places.status_note: Janet Echelman's 'Bending Arc' sculpture is marked temporarily closed on the Pier's map (checked 2026-09-27).
places.accessibility: Three ADA-compliant trams with four stops, accessible for wheelchairs and walkers; the Coastal Thicket boardwalk is ADA accessible.
places.parking_text: More than 500 paid spaces in the Dolphin and Pelican lots (6-hour maximum; $2/hour weekdays, $2.50/hour weekends for the first 4 hours); overflow at the Sundial garage and Al Lang lot; free Downtown Looper trolley.

places.name: Tampa Bay Watch Discovery Center
places.hours_text: Daily 10am–5pm; holiday exceptions listed on the site.
places.price_text: Adults and teens 13+ $8; seniors 60+ $6; military, Florida teachers and children 4–12 $3; 3 and under free.
places.summary: Small nature center on the St. Pete Pier's over-water walkway, run by the nonprofit Tampa Bay Watch, with interactive exhibits on the Tampa Bay estuary, live animals, a touch tank, daily programs and wildlife boat tours.
places.quote: Our exhibit gallery features interactive displays, live animals, and a touch tank for hands-on learning.
places.parking_text: Pier Pelican lot (paid), first come, first served; Pier trams stop at the center.

places.name: Grand Central District
places.summary: Main Street district along Central Avenue from 16th to 31st Street, just west of downtown, with more than 350 independent shops, restaurants, bars and galleries and many murals. The association calls it the birthplace of St. Pete's Pride Parade; it hosts Halloween on Central and a Christmas market.
places.quote: Founded in 2000 and located just west of downtown St. Petersburg, the Grand Central District is home to over 350 locally owned and operated independent businesses
places.notes: Point is the 2200 block of Central Avenue, mid-district (a representative point, not an address of the association).

places.name: Central Arts District
places.summary: Downtown stretch of Central Avenue from 3rd to 7th Street with murals, galleries and museums (Florida CraftArt, the Chihuly Collection, the Morean Arts Center), boutiques, restaurants, bars and music venues such as Jannus Live and the Floridian Social Club.
places.quote: runs along Central Avenue in downtown St. Pete, extending from 3rd Street to 7th Street (locals will refer to it as the 300 block to the 700 block)
places.notes: No district association site found; the Visit St. Pete/Clearwater district page is the source. Point is the 500 block of Central Avenue.

places.name: EDGE District
places.address: Central Avenue between 9th Street (MLK) and 16th Street
places.summary: Walkable Main Street district on Central Avenue between 9th Street (MLK) and 16th Street, with locally owned bars, restaurants and shops, between downtown and the Grand Central District.
places.quote: The EDGE District runs along St. Pete's Central Avenue between 9th Street (MLK) & 16th Street, and outward to both 1st Ave North & 1st Ave South.
places.notes: Point is the 1200 block of Central Avenue, mid-district.

places.name: Warehouse Arts District
places.summary: Former industrial area south of Central Avenue (roughly 16th to 31st Street, 1st Avenue North to 10th Avenue South) with artist studios, glass and clay studios, galleries and breweries. The Warehouse Arts District Association's ArtsXchange campus holds studios and galleries and hosts the Second Saturday ArtWalk.
places.quote: The Warehouse Arts District features a collection of artist studios, galleries and events on the campus of ArtsXchange in St. Petersburg, FL.
places.notes: Boundaries from the Visit St. Pete/Clearwater district page. warehouseartsdistrictstpete.com is a hijacked domain (gambling spam) as of 2026-09-27: do not link it.

places.name: Beach Drive
places.summary: Downtown waterfront street along the bayfront parks, lined with restaurants with outdoor seating, bars and shops; it anchors what Visit St. Pete/Clearwater calls the Waterfront Museum District, between Beach Drive and 3rd Street from 7th Avenue South to 7th Avenue North, home to the Dalí, the MFA and other museums.
places.quote: You'll find St. Pete's Waterfront Museum District between Beach Drive and 3rd St., stretching from 7th Avenue South to 7th Avenue North.
places.notes: beachdrive.com is a commercial directory for the street, not an official body. Point is 300 Beach Dr NE.

places.name: The Deuces (22nd Street South)
places.summary: Corridor on 22nd Street South that was the center of St. Petersburg's Black business community during segregation, with hundreds of Black-owned businesses at its peak in the early 1960s. The Deuces Live Main Street program has worked on its revival since 2012; the Woodson African American Museum and murals are here.
places.quote: During segregation, 22nd Street South — lovingly known as “The Deuces” — became a hub of Black excellence, creativity, and commerce.
places.notes: Point is the Deuces Live office, 833 22nd Street South. history-region may also hold this corridor as a historic district; merge by id if so.

places.name: Duncan McClellan Gallery
places.hours_text: Monday–Saturday 11am–6pm, Sunday noon–4pm.
places.summary: Glass art gallery in the Warehouse Arts District with rotating shows of national and international glass artists, in a former fish and tomato packing plant with courtyards and sculpture gardens.
places.quote: The Duncan McClellan Gallery, located in St. Petersburg Florida, features rotating exhibitions showcasing national and internationally recognized glass artists.
places.notes: The home page lists two hours blocks (Mon–Sat 11–6 in one place, plus Sundays noon–4 in the footer).

places.name: FloridaRAMA
places.hours_text: Monday, Thursday and Friday noon–8pm; Saturday and Sunday 10am–8pm; closed Tuesday and Wednesday. Last entry 90 minutes before closing.
places.price_text: Ticketed; the art gallery is free.
places.summary: Indoor, ticketed immersive art installation about Florida stories, made by more than 80 mostly local artists, with scavenger-hunt games, a shop, a snack bar and a free gallery. It is inside Building 5 of The Factory St. Pete in the Warehouse Arts District.
places.quote: Cooler than a museum, smarter than a theme park, and weirder than a carnival, FloridaRAMA is an immersive art experience located in St. Pete’s Warehouse Arts District.
places.accessibility: Indoor and ADA accessible, per the site; ADA parking on the Pinellas Trail side.
places.parking_text: Free parking in The Factory's north lot (Fairfield Ave S) and south lot (7th Ave S), plus street parking; on the Pinellas Trail with bike parking.
places.notes: Ticket prices are not printed on the pages read (sold through the ticketing link). thefactorystpete.com now redirects to floridarama.art; the site's news page cites 'Fairgrounds St. Pete expands and rebrands as FloridaRAMA', and the footer says it is operated by Fairgrounds Projects Inc. The Factory itself (a campus of studios and galleries) was not given its own record because its own site no longer describes it.

places.name: Zen Glass Studio & Gallery
places.hours_text: Tuesday–Saturday 10am–5pm; Second Saturday 10am–9pm.
places.summary: Glass studio and gallery in the Warehouse Arts District, founded in 2002 by artists David Walker and Josh Poll, selling blown and sculpted glass and jewelry and teaching flameworking and glassblowing classes. Visitors can walk into the studio from the 6th Avenue South side.
places.quote: They feature a huge selection of blown and sculpted glass art, jewelry and sculpture in the gallery.

places.name: Saturday Morning Market
places.address: Al Lang Stadium parking lot, 1st Street South
places.hours_text: Saturdays 9am–2pm, October through May, at Al Lang Stadium; a smaller summer market runs 9am–1pm; no market in September.
places.price_text: Free admission.
places.summary: Weekly open-air market, running since 2002, with local farmers, ready-to-eat food from many cuisines, seafood, baked goods, local artists and live music. The fall-to-spring season is held in the Al Lang Stadium lot downtown.
places.quote: Since 2002, the Saturday Morning Market has been a cornerstone of the St. Petersburg community, bringing together residents and visitors in a vibrant celebration of local food, art, music, and connection.
places.status_note: On its September break; returns to Al Lang Stadium on Saturday, Oct 3, 2026 for the October–May season (per ilovetheburg.com, Sep 1, 2026). The 2026 summer market was held at St. Pete First United Methodist Church, 212 3rd Street North, because of construction at Williams Park.
places.parking_text: Nearby parking garages and city street parking.
places.notes: saturdaymorningmarket.com returned a bot-check (HTTP 202, empty) to curl and WebFetch on 2026-09-27; facts are from a dated local news article and the St. Petersburg Chamber's event page. Point is Al Lang Stadium (OSM).

places.name: Tyrone Square
places.summary: Simon shopping mall in west St. Petersburg with more than 55 stores (including Macy's, Dick's Sporting Goods and H&M) and more than 10 restaurants.
places.quote: St. Petersburg's Family-Favorite Shopping Destination. 55+ Stores. 10+ Restaurants.
places.notes: Weekly hours were not shown on the page as read (only the current day's hours), so hours_text is null.

places.name: Crislip Arcade
places.summary: Renovated 1926 open-air shopping arcade on the 600 block of Central Avenue: a covered walkway lined with small independent shops.
places.quote: A renovated 1926 shopping arcade located on the 600 block of Central Avenue, which is an open-air, covered hallway with a string of small retails shops on either side.
places.notes: No official site found. Point is the OpenStreetMap feature for the arcade (tagged 645 Central Avenue); the source says only "600 block".

places.name: St. Petersburg Shuffleboard Club
places.hours_text: Open play Tuesday and Thursday 6–9pm, Friday 7–10pm (Friday night St. Pete Shuffle), Sunday 9am–noon.
places.price_text: Open hours free for members, $10 per non-member; kids free.
places.summary: Shuffleboard club at Mirror Lake, organized in 1924 by six players as what the club calls the first strictly shuffleboard club in the world; the game's official rules were written here in the late 1920s. Visitors can play during open hours, including Friday nights.
places.quote: So in 1924 a group of shuffleboard players — six in this case — organized what they called the Mirror Lake Park Shuffleboard Club, the first strictly shuffleboard club in the world
places.notes: history-region may also hold this as a historic site; merge by id.

places.name: Gulfport Waterfront District
places.summary: Small historic downtown on Boca Ciega Bay along Beach Boulevard (below 28th Avenue South) and Shore Boulevard, with murals, independent galleries, boutiques and more than a dozen restaurants, a fishing pier, a small beach, the historic Casino ballroom, a twice-monthly Art Walk and the Tuesday Fresh Market.
places.quote: The twice-monthly Art Walk transforms Beach Boulevard into an open-air gallery.
places.notes: Source is the Gulfport Merchants Chamber (visitgulfportflorida.com). The City of Gulfport site (mygulfport.us) returned a bot-check on 2026-09-27. Point is the Gulfport Casino at the foot of Beach Blvd (OSM); the Casino ballroom itself belongs to venues-bay.

places.name: Gulfport History Museum
places.hours_text: Wednesday 10am–2pm, Thursday noon–4pm, Friday 10am–2pm, 1st and 3rd Saturdays noon–4pm.
places.price_text: Free.
places.summary: Small free museum of the history of Gulfport, which the listing calls one of Pinellas County's oldest incorporated cities.
places.quote: This museum documents the diversity and colorful history of one of Pinellas County's oldest incorporated cities.
places.notes: The city's museum page (mygulfport.us) returned a bot-check on 2026-09-27; facts are from the Visit St. Pete/Clearwater listing. gulfportmuseum.org is a different Gulfport (Mississippi).

places.name: Penny Lane Beatles Museum
places.hours_text: Wednesday 10am–4pm; Thursday–Sunday 11am–3pm.
places.price_text: Free admission.
places.summary: Free downtown museum of a local collector's Beatles memorabilia, more than 1,000 pieces dating back to 1961. The listing calls it the only permanent Beatles exhibit in the United States.
places.quote: PENNY LANE, Beatles Museum is the brainchild of a long-time Dunedin resident and humanitarian who considers the time is right to share his eclectic collection of Beatles memorabilia covering several decades dating back to 1961.
places.notes: The museum's own site returned a bot-check (HTTP 202) on 2026-09-27; verifier should confirm hours there.

places.name: John's Pass Village & Boardwalk
places.hours_text: Open daily; individual shop and restaurant hours vary.
places.summary: Waterfront boardwalk village at John's Pass with more than 100 shops, restaurants and water-related businesses: the local fishing fleet, dolphin and shelling tours, pirate ship cruises, boat rentals, parasailing and jet skis. The beach is a short walk away.
places.quote: Over one hundred merchants inhabit the Village with unique retail shopping, a variety of restaurants, the local fishing fleet, dolphin watching and shelling tours, boat rentals, parasailing and jet skiing.
places.status_note: Visit St. Pete/Clearwater's listing says the village is still recovering from the 2024 hurricanes, with some areas (such as the lower decks of certain restaurants) temporarily closed while the boardwalk operates (checked 2026-09-27).
places.parking_text: Pay-by-meter garage at the southwest corner and two pay-by-meter lots (Central lot and Beach lot).
places.notes: johnspass.com is the 'Discover John's Pass' merchant site (it calls the village 'Pinellas County’s #1 tourist attraction'). Phone and parking from the VSPC listing.

places.name: Pier 60
places.hours_text: Pier 7am–10pm; park 6am–9pm daily. Sunsets at Pier 60 runs nightly from 2 hours before to 2 hours after sunset, weather permitting.
places.summary: A 1,080-foot fishing pier with a bait house, next to a beachfront park with a large beach playground, covered pavilions and telescopes. Sunsets at Pier 60, a free nightly festival of artisans and street performers held since 1995, takes place in the park.
places.quote: Sunsets at Pier 60 debuted on March 17, 1995 as a year-round nightly sunset celebration on the iconic Pier 60.
places.notes: Fishing fees were not stated on the pages read. No closure notice was found on the city's beach page (which invites visitors to 'go fishing on Pier 60'); the verifier should confirm the pier's post-2024 status on myclearwater.com if a Pier 60 page exists. Animals are not permitted on Pier 60 or the bathing beaches (service dogs excepted), per sunsetsatpier60.com.

places.name: Clearwater Marine Aquarium
places.hours_text: Daily 10am–5pm; last entry 30 minutes before closing. Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas; 9am–3pm Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve.
places.price_text: Adults (12+) $41.95; kids 3–11 $32.95; seniors 65+ $39.95; 2 and under free.
places.summary: Nonprofit aquarium and marine animal hospital just off the Memorial Causeway (via Island Way) between downtown Clearwater and the beach; it rescues, rehabilitates and releases marine life, and visitors see resident dolphins, sea turtles and other rescued animals. Its site keeps a 'Remembering Winter' page for Winter the dolphin.
places.quote: Clearwater Marine Aquarium is a working animal hospital dedicated to the rescue. rehabilitation, and release of marine life and a leader in research and conservation efforts to protect animals in the wild.
places.parking_text: Paid garage at the aquarium (seasonal rates; members discounted); ticketing is on the garage's 3rd level entrance.
places.notes: Area follows SPEC §4.1 (downtown-clearwater includes 'the aquarium').

places.name: Clearwater Beach Marina
places.summary: City marina on Causeway Boulevard at Clearwater Beach, the departure point for fishing and sailing charters, sightseeing boats, dinner cruises, dolphin tours, parasailing and personal watercraft rentals, with restaurants, shops and a bait house.
places.quote: The fishing fleet and dinner boats are currently in temporary locations, but continue to be fully operational and accessible.
places.status_note: Under a two-phase replacement project expected to finish in August 2026; tourism boats operate from new slips along Coronado Drive and there are no transient or day docks (per the City of Clearwater, checked 2026-09-27).

places.name: Beach Walk
places.address: South Gulfview Boulevard, south of Pier 60
places.summary: Landscaped, winding beachside promenade on Clearwater Beach running south from Pier 60, with views of the beach.
places.quote: Beach Walk is located to the south of Pier 60 and is a winding beachside promenade with lush landscaping, artistic touches and clear views of the beach.

places.name: Seaside Seabird Sanctuary
places.hours_text: Daily 9am–5pm.
places.price_text: Admission and parking free.
places.summary: Avian hospital and sanctuary on 1.5 beachfront acres that rescues and rehabilitates native wild birds; visitors see more than 100 resident birds, the hospital at work, a gift shop and an observation deck over the Gulf.
places.quote: We are an Avian Rehabilitation Hospital & Sanctuary dedicated to the care of sick, injured, & orphaned native wild birds!
places.status_note: The sanctuary reported about 4 feet of storm surge through all its buildings in the 2024 hurricanes (post of Jan 13, 2025); its visit page now lists daily hours.
places.notes: The home page teaser says 'open every day from 8-4' while the visit page and site header say 9am–5pm; the visit page is used. seabirdsanctuary.org and seasidesanctuary.org are unrelated sites; do not link them.

places.name: Indian Rocks Historical Museum
places.hours_text: Wednesday–Saturday 10am–2pm.
places.price_text: Free; donations requested.
places.summary: Local history museum in a historic beach cottage in Chic-a-Si Park, covering the beach from prehistoric times through pioneer settlement to the motel and condo eras, with old photographs and a gift shop.
places.quote: Come discover the history and stories of Indian Rocks Beach!
places.accessibility: Wheelchair accessible, with accessible parking and restrooms, per the listing.

places.name: Palm Harbor Museum
places.hours_text: Thursday, Friday and Saturday 10am–2pm; closed on holidays.
places.price_text: Free or donation; docent-led or self-guided.
places.summary: Small museum of the history of Palm Harbor, Crystal Beach, Ozona and Curlew from 1800s settlement to today, in a house built around 1915, at the corner of Belcher and Curlew roads.
places.quote: We welcome you! Free/Donation Tours can be docent-led or self-guided
places.parking_text: Free parking; enter from Curlew Road.
places.notes: Hours differ: the museum's site says Thu–Sat 10–2, Visit St. Pete/Clearwater says Wed–Fri 10–2; the museum's own site is used. The ~1915 house date is from the VSPC listing.

places.name: Clearwater Historical Society Museum and Cultural Center
places.hours_text: Wednesday–Saturday 10am–2pm; private tours by arrangement.
places.price_text: Free; donations encouraged.
places.summary: History museum on the five-acre campus of the former South Ward School (opened 1906), open since June 2019, with exhibits on Clearwater's founding families, local restaurants and schools. The society also runs the Plumb House Museum.
places.quote: The Clearwater Historical Society Museum and Cultural Center is located on the five-acre campus of the historic South Ward School at 610 South Fort Harrison Avenue in Clearwater.
places.notes: Free admission from the VSPC listing; the 1906 school opening year from the VSPC listing.

places.name: DK Farms & Gardens

places.name: Dunedin History Museum
places.hours_text: Monday–Saturday 11am–5pm, Sunday noon–4pm.
places.price_text: Adults $5; ages 13–17, seniors, college students and teachers $4; visitors with disabilities $3; under 12 free; members free.
places.summary: Local history museum in downtown Dunedin, in the town's former railroad depot (a station site since 1888; the current building dates from 1924 and served trains until 1987). The museum says the railroad boosted the citrus industry and tourism; its old line is now the Pinellas Trail.

places.name: Dunedin Fine Art Center
places.hours_text: Monday–Friday 9am–5pm, Saturday–Sunday 10am–2pm. DLM Children's Museum: Monday–Friday 10am–5pm, Saturday–Sunday 10am–2pm.

places.name: Downtown Dunedin (Main Street)

places.name: Sunshine Skyway Bridge
places.address: I-275 / US 19 over Lower Tampa Bay
places.price_text: Toll bridge (I-275 / US 19).
places.summary: Cable-stayed toll bridge carrying I-275 and US 19 across Lower Tampa Bay from St. Petersburg to Manatee County, about 4.1 miles long with a 1,200-foot main span; the current bridge opened in 1987. It replaced the original Skyway, part of which fell in 1980 when a freighter struck it.

heritage.story: The first Sunshine Skyway, a two-lane bridge, was completed in 1954, and a second two-lane span opened in 1971. On May 9, 1980, the freighter Summit Venture struck a support pier during a squall; the southbound roadway collapsed and 35 people died. The present cable-stayed bridge, designed by Figg & Muller Engineering Group and built by the American Bridge Company, opened in 1987, and the old bridge was partly demolished and turned into two fishing piers.
heritage.visiting: You see it by driving across (a toll applies) or from the two long fishing piers made from the old bridge.
